q: The maximal equicontinuous factor of a minimal topological dynamical system (X,T) is the quotient by the proximal relation P and the regionally proximal relation RP. For a distal system:
opts: The system IS its own maximal equicontinuous factor
P = {(x,x)} (no non-trivial proximal pairs), and the maximal equicontinuous factor equals the system if it is equicontinuous
The system has no equicontinuous factor
exp: For a distal system (no non-trivial proximal pairs), P = Δ (diagonal). The maximal equicontinuous factor of an equicontinuous distal system is the system itself — a group rotation. For general distal systems, the equicontinuous structure relation (= RP) determines the maximal equicontinuous factor.
